evidence.source: KORG padKONTROL MIDI Implementation + Owner's Manual + EasyStart: pads/knobs/XY/pedal are ALL assignable per scene; pads default to MIDI ch 10; factory pad NOTES are scene-based (30 preload scenes), no fixed factory note table is published - so the GM drum map below is a SUGGESTION the console can re-learn, not a factory transcription

firmware_basis: standard MIDI mode (not native KORG SysEx)
notes: Pads default to MIDI channel 10 (profile channel set to match). The keyboard block renders exactly the 16 pad notes so the on-screen piano plays the kit too.

Pad NOTES here are a General-Midi drum suggestion (36..51): the padKONTROL has no fixed factory note table - every scene assigns its own. Play a pad and the console passive-learns the REAL number, or rebind from the edit menu.

Knob 1/2, the X-Y pad (X/Y) and the pedal jack are fully assignable in the device's Setting mode - the CCs here (16/17, 18/19, 20) are starting points; rebind in the console after assigning on the device.
The device appears as TWO MIDI ports (Port A / Port B). One profile binds one bus: if your scene splits pads across ports, point the bus at Port A or use a Port A+B scene.

Left keys (TYPE, OFF VAL, VELOCITY, PORT, FIX.VEL, SWAP, X-PAD, SCENE) and right keys (HOLD, FLAM, ROLL, PEDAL, KNOB1, KNOB2, Y-PAD) are Setting-mode selectors - they send no MIDI in standard mode, so they cannot be bound.
Pad LEDs are scene-driven (native SysEx only) - the console does not write them.
